Course heavily depends on Mathematics and some fundamental ideas to be learnt and remembered. However, in the lectures it is more about understanding how this example can be solved or what is the way to solve it to memorize it and use it every time instead of understanding why we are doing it. This course is really fun and challenging if you can really understand it, but with Mr. Dibeklioğlu, it is certainly not.

*   Sometimes, during the lectures, the instructor states what he expects in exams (e.g. the format of the answers and amount of detail expected in those answers). However,  classwork exams are graded by the TAs in totally different ways. The instructor expects one sort of answer while the TAs expect some other kind. Consequently, I lost so many points for no reason (just because of following what the instructor said in lectures). For instance, in "pumping lemma" questions, the instructor said that we could write informal descriptions to explain different cases; however, the TA expected formal explanations for each case while evaluating the exams. For that reason, the TA cut too many points from those who followed what the instructor said, including me. In short, although I knew the subject very well, I lost significantly many points due to the inconsistency between the instructor and the TAs.

*   The instructor does not give enough time for quizzes. Although he solves each quiz question on the board (and shows that a quick solution was possible), his solutions miss so many details. Normally, if a TA was to evaluate his quiz answers, the instructor could not get a full grade. Again, for that reason, even though I could do better on quizzes, due to the given time's being too limited, I could not get grades that I deserve.

*    Overall, I feel that the instructor (and TAs) could not assess my knowledge properly. I could not obtain grades that are worthy of my hard work. I feel like most of my work is just wasted.
